   114	            for binding in scope.values_mut() {
   115	                binding.fields.retain(|key, _| match key.first().map(String::as_str) {
   116	                    Some(POINT) => safe && key.get(1) == Some(table) && key.get(2)
   117	                        .and_then(|index| definition.index(index)).is_some_and(|index|
   118	                            !fields.iter().any(|field| index.columns().contains(&field.name)
   119	                                || key.iter().skip(3).any(|part| part.starts_with(&format!("Some({:?}):", field.name))))),
   120	                    Some(maintain_types::AUTHORIZATION) => false,
   121	                    Some(aggregate_facts::NONEMPTY) => false,
   122	                    Some(aggregate_facts::COUNT_CAPTURE) => false,
   123	                    _ => true,
   124	                });
   125	            }
   126	        }
   127	    }
   128	
   129	    pub(super) fn ordinary_write_lifetime(&self, table: &str) -> bool {
   130	        self.schema.table(table).is_some_and(|table| table.expire.is_none()
   131	            && table.not_before.is_none() && table.through.is_none() && table.ephemeral.is_none())
   132	    }
   133	
   134	    pub(super) fn row_independent_read_proved(&self, table: &str) -> bool {
   135	        let Some(info) = self.catalog.tables.get(table) else { return false };
   136	        if self.schema.tables[table].rules.read.is_uniformly_readable() { return true; }
   137	        let Some(rule) = info.decl.rules.iter().find(|rule| rule.effect == ast::Effect::Read) else { return false };
   138	        fn proved(binder: &Binder<'_>, table: &str, value: &A) -> bool {
   139	            if let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = value && op == "or" {
   140	                return proved(binder, table, left) || proved(binder, table, right);
   141	            }
   142	            let mut value = value.clone();
   143	            maintain_types::normalize_rule_constants(&mut value);
   144	            let mut row_dependent = false;
   145	            super::super::intent_walk::expression(&mut value, &mut |expr| {
   146	                if matches!(expr, A::Focal { .. }) { row_dependent = true; }
   147	                if let A::Call { name, .. } = expr && binder.catalog.functions.contains_key(name) {
   148	                    row_dependent = true;
   149	                }
   150	                if let A::Read(read) | A::Exists { read, .. } | A::Created { read, .. } = expr {
   151	                    row_dependent |= read.table == table || binder.catalog.tables.get(&read.table)
   152	                        .is_none_or(|info| info.maintained.is_some())
   153	                        || binder.schema.table(&read.table).is_none_or(|target| !target.maintained.is_empty() || target.through.is_some());
   154	                }
   155	            });
   156	            !row_dependent && binder.point_guard_safe(&value) && binder.authorization_proved(&value, true)
   157	        }
   158	        proved(self, table, &rule.value)
   159	    }
   160	
   161	    pub(super) fn parent_rewrite(&self, value: &A) -> Option<String> {
   162	        let A::Member { base, name, .. } = value else { return None; };
   163	        let A::Read(read) = base.as_ref() else { return None; };
   164	        let info = self.catalog.tables.get(&read.table)?;
   165	        let field = Ty::from_scalar(info.columns.get(name)?);
   166	        if self.point_present(read) || field.is_optional() || info.maintained.is_some()
   167	            || info.decl.columns.iter().any(|c| c.name == *name && c.written_by.is_some() && !c.readable_by_audience) { return None; }
   168	        Some(format!("require exists {} else NOT_FOUND — a membership or required reference does not prove this row exists; alternatively bind {} ! else NOT_FOUND", print::read_expr(read), print::read_expr(read)))
   169	    }
   170	}
   171	
   172	pub(super) fn writes(body: &[Stmt]) -> bool {
   173	    ir::effects::Effects::writes_in(body)
   174	}
   175	
   176	fn rule_probes(rule: &snapback4_core::schema::RuleExpr, target: &str) -> bool {
   177	    use snapback4_core::schema::RuleExpr;
   178	    match rule {
   179	        RuleExpr::Exists { table, .. } | RuleExpr::Created { table, .. } => table == target,
   180	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().any(|rule| rule_probes(rule, target)),
   181	        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => rule_probes(rule, target),
   182	        _ => false,
   183	    }
   184	}
   185	
   186	fn rule_dependencies_stable(schema: &snapback4_core::schema::Schema, rule: &snapback4_core::schema::RuleExpr) -> bool {
   187	    use snapback4_core::schema::RuleExpr;
   188	    match rule {
   189	        RuleExpr::Exists { table, .. } | RuleExpr::Created { table, .. } => schema.table(table)
   190	            .is_some_and(|target| target.maintained.is_empty() && target.through.is_none() && schema.maintain_for(table).is_none()),
   191	        RuleExpr::And(items) | RuleExpr::Or(items) => items.iter().all(|rule| rule_dependencies_stable(schema, rule)),
   192	        RuleExpr::Not(rule) => rule_dependencies_stable(schema, rule),
   193	        _ => true,
   194	    }
   195	}
     1	//! Null facts for repeated, effect-free helper calls over lexical snapshots.
     2	use super::*;
     3	use std::collections::BTreeSet;
     4	
     5	pub(super) const CONSTANTS: &str = "$pureCallConstants";
     6	
     7	#[derive(Debug)]
     8	pub(super) enum Stable {
     9	    Literal(String),
    10	    Snapshot(String, Vec<String>),
    11	    Viewer,
    12	    Call(String, Vec<Stable>),
    13	}
    14	
    15	impl Binder<'_> {
    16	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.2 — a repeated pure call narrows like a snapshot field.
    17	    // Facts live on *every* argument root so the existing branch intersections,
    18	    // reassignment invalidation and loop fixed point apply to them as to fields.
    19	    fn stable_call(&self, value: &A) -> Option<(Vec<String>, BTreeSet<String>)> {
    20	        if !matches!(value, A::Call { .. }) { return None; }
    21	        let mut roots = BTreeSet::new();
    22	        let stable = self.stable_value(value, &mut roots)?;
    23	        if roots.is_empty() { roots.insert(CONSTANTS.into()); }
    24	        Some((vec!["$pureCall".into(), stable.key()], roots))
    25	    }
    26	
    27	    pub(super) fn stable_value(&self, value: &A, roots: &mut BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<Stable> {
    28	        match value {
    29	            A::Literal { .. } => Some(Stable::Literal(print::expression(value))),
    30	            A::Name { name, .. } if name == "viewer" => Some(Stable::Viewer),
    31	            A::Name { name, .. } if matches!(name.as_str(), "now" | "commit" | "new") => None,
    32	            A::Name { .. } | A::Member { .. } | A::Focal { .. } => {
    33	                let (root, path) = control::field_path(value, self.focal.as_ref().map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()))?;
    34	                let runtime = if let Some(binding) = self.binding(&root) {
    35	                    roots.insert(root.clone());
    36	                    binding.runtime.clone()
    37	                } else {
    38	                    // A shape's implicit row is an immutable lexical snapshot.
    39	                    // Its unique runtime identity separates projection scopes;
    40	                    // with no mutable argument roots, use the constant anchor.
    41	                    self.focal.as_ref().filter(|(name, _)| name == &root)?.0.clone()
    42	                };
    43	                Some(Stable::Snapshot(runtime, path))
    44	            }
    45	            A::Call { name, args, .. } => {
    46	                let function = self.catalog.functions.get(name)?;
    47	                if !self.pure_functions.get(&function.name).copied().unwrap_or(false) { return None; }
    48	                Some(Stable::Call(function.name.clone(), args.iter().map(|arg| self.stable_value(arg, roots)).collect::<Option<_>>()?))
    49	            }
    50	            _ => None,
    51	        }
    52	    }
    53	
    54	    pub(super) fn narrow_call(&mut self, value: &A, present: bool) {
    55	        let Some((key, roots)) = self.stable_call(value) else { return; };
    56	        let Some(ty) = self.call_types.get(&key) else { return; };
    57	        let ty = if present { ty.required() } else { Ty::Null };
    58	        for root in roots {
    59	            let mut binding = self.binding(&root).expect("a stable root").clone();
    60	            binding.fields.insert(key.clone(), ty.clone());
    61	            self.scopes.last_mut().expect("a scope").insert(root, binding);
    62	        }
    63	    }
    64	
    65	    pub(super) fn record_call(&mut self, value: &A, ty: &Ty) {
    66	        if let Some((key, _)) = self.stable_call(value) { self.call_types.insert(key, ty.clone()); }
    67	    }
    68	
    69	    pub(super) fn call_refinement(&self, value: &A) -> Option<Ty> {
    70	        let (key, roots) = self.stable_call(value)?;
    71	        let mut result = None;
    72	        for root in roots {
    73	            let ty = self.binding(&root)?.fields.get(&key)?;
    74	            if result.as_ref().is_some_and(|other| other != ty) { return None; }
    75	            result = Some(ty.clone());
    76	        }
    77	        result
    78	    }
    79	}
    80	
    81	impl Stable {
    82	    // Escaped serialization of the structured identity, never source
    83	    // sites or helper temporaries. Argument order and snapshot identity matter.
    84	    pub(super) fn key(&self) -> String {
    85	        match self {
    86	            Self::Literal(value) => format!("literal:{value:?}"),
    87	            Self::Snapshot(root, path) => format!("snapshot:{root:?}:{path:?}"),
    88	            Self::Viewer => "viewer".into(),
    89	            Self::Call(name, args) => format!("call:{name:?}:{:?}", args.iter().map(Self::key).collect::<Vec<_>>()),
    90	        }
    91	    }
    92	}
    93	
    94	// Inspect expanded IR, after argument setup: this covers transitive helpers,
    95	// named shapes, aggregates and reads hidden in blocks without a second AST
    96	// effect model. It only classifies effects; calls still execute and are metered.
    97	pub(super) fn expression(value: &Expr) -> bool {
    98	    match value {
    99	        Expr::Literal(_) | Expr::Variable(_) | Expr::Input(Input::Viewer) => true,
   100	        Expr::Input(Input::Now | Input::ReadTime | Input::NewId) => false,
   101	        Expr::Get(_) | Expr::Exists(_) | Expr::Scan(_) | Expr::Merge(_) => false,
   102	        Expr::Field { base, .. } | Expr::Unary { value: base, .. } => expression(base),
   103	        Expr::Array(values) => values.iter().all(expression),
   104	        Expr::Object(fields) => fields.values().all(expression),
   105	        Expr::Shape { base, fields } => expression(base) && fields.values().all(expression),
   106	        Expr::Binary { left, right, .. } => expression(left) && expression(right),
   107	        Expr::Builtin { builtin, args } => builtin_pure(builtin) && args.iter().all(expression),
   108	        Expr::Block { body, value } => statements(body) && expression(value),
   109	    }
   110	}
   111	
   112	fn builtin_pure(builtin: &Builtin) -> bool {
   113	    match builtin {
   114	        Builtin::RequireUncapped => false,
   115	        Builtin::JobAs | Builtin::JobQuery { .. } => false,
   116	        Builtin::Connected | Builtin::ReceiptSettled { .. } => false,
   117	        Builtin::ProjectFields { .. } | Builtin::OptionalField { .. } | Builtin::Calendar { .. } | Builtin::Civil(_)
   118	        | Builtin::Len | Builtin::Slice | Builtin::Concat | Builtin::Lower | Builtin::Trim
   119	        | Builtin::Sha256 | Builtin::Join | Builtin::Group { .. } | Builtin::First | Builtin::Last
   120	        | Builtin::At | Builtin::Min | Builtin::Max | Builtin::Extremum { .. }
   121	        | Builtin::ExtremumOf { .. } | Builtin::Divmod { .. } | Builtin::Divide { .. } | Builtin::Sort { .. }
   122	        | Builtin::MentionTokens | Builtin::SearchPresent | Builtin::DeterministicShare
   123	        | Builtin::Count | Builtin::Sum | Builtin::CountCapped => true,
   124	    }
   125	}

   183	  return owner
   184	mutation staleDomain(owner: principal, victim: entries):
   185	  n = count(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner)
   186	  require n > 0 else EMPTY
   187	  return min(entries[changingOwner(owner, victim)] by byOwner, .score) + 1
   188	"#))]);
   189	    assert!(impure_domain.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
   190	        "writeful domains must never be replayed as aggregate proof: {:#?}", impure_domain.diagnostics);
   191	
   192	    let shadowed = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{schema}
   193	fn count(owner: principal):
   194	  return 1
   195	query shadowedCount(owner: principal):
   196	  n = count(owner)
   197	  require n > 0 else EMPTY
   198	  return min(entries[owner] by byOwner, .score) + 1
   199	"#))]);
   200	    assert!(shadowed.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE" && d.message.contains("int ?")),
   201	        "a user helper named count must not create builtin provenance: {:#?}", shadowed.diagnostics);
   202	}

   205	fn matching_role_guard_narrows_only_the_authorized_keyed_total() {
   206	    let source = r#"

   210	  online only
   211	table staff:
   212	  principal: principal
   213	  role: enum('finance')
   214	  unique principal, role
   215	  read <- .principal = viewer
   216	  delete <- .principal = viewer
   217	  online only
   218	view totals: count entries by .owner
   219	  read <- exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
   220	  online only
   221	query raw(owner: principal):
   222	  return totals[owner]
   223	query guarded(owner: principal):
   224	  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
   225	  return totals[owner] + 1
   226	"#;
   227	    let bound = checked(source);
   228	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|program| program.program.name == "raw").unwrap().result, Ty::Int.optional());

   231	    engine.seed([("entries".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
   232	        ("id", Value::Id("one".into())), ("owner", Value::Id("bob".into())),
   233	    ]))]).unwrap();
   234	    let raw = |engine: &mut Engine, owner: &str| engine.query("raw", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
   235	        ("owner".into(), Value::Id(owner.into())),
   236	    ]))).unwrap().data;
   237	    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Null, "a hidden stored total is not disclosed");
   238	    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Null, "a hidden miss is indistinguishable from a hidden hit");
   239	    engine.seed([("staff".into(), snapback4_core::value::object([
   240	        ("id", Value::Id("finance".into())), ("principal", Value::Id("alice".into())),
   241	        ("role", Value::String("finance".into())),
   242	    ]))]).unwrap();
   243	    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "bob"), Value::Int(1));
   244	    assert_eq!(raw(&mut engine, "nobody"), Value::Int(0), "an authorized keyed miss has the count identity");
   245	    assert_eq!(engine.query("guarded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
   246	        ("owner".into(), Value::Id("nobody".into())),
   247	    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1));
   248	
   249	    let stale = compile(&[("schema.q".into(), format!(r#"{source}
   250	mutation stale(owner: principal, grant: staff):
   251	  require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance'] else NOT_FINANCE
   252	  delete staff[grant]
   253	  return totals[owner] + 1
   254	"#))]);
   255	    assert!(stale.diagnostics.iter().any(|diagnostic| diagnostic.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"
   256	        && diagnostic.message.contains("int ?")), "a write must invalidate the role proof: {:#?}", stale.diagnostics);

   312	fn rounded_division_is_exact_signed_and_keeps_numeric_types() {

   317	    divide(5, 2, 'floor'), divide(5, 2, 'ceiling'),
   318	    divide(5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'), divide(5, 2, 'half-even'),
   319	    divide(7, 2, 'half-even'), divide(-5, 2, 'half-away-from-zero'),
   320	    divide(-5, 2, 'floor'), divide(-5, 2, 'ceiling'),
   321	    divide(5, -2, 'floor'), divide(5, -2, 'ceiling'),
   322	    divide(7, 3, 'half-even'), divide(8, 3, 'half-even')
   323	  ]
   324	query decimalValue(value: decimal 2):
   325	  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
   326	query moneyValue(value: money USD 2):
   327	  return divide(value, 2, 'half-even')
   328	query scaled(numerator: int, denominator: int):
   329	  return [
   330	    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-even'),
   331	    divide(numerator, denominator, 2, 'half-away-from-zero')
   332	  ]
   333	query wide(numerator: int, denominator: int):
   334	  return divide(numerator, denominator, 12, 'half-even')
   335	query scaleZero(numerator: int, denominator: int):
   336	  return divide(numerator, denominator, 0, 'half-even')
   337	query scaledOverflow():
   338	  return divide(9007199254740991, 1, 1, 'half-even')
   339	query zero():
   340	  return divide(1, 0, 'half-even')
   341	"#;
   342	    let bound = checked(source);
   343	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "decimalValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Decimal(2));
   344	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "moneyValue").unwrap().result, Ty::Money("USD".into(), 2));
   345	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "scaled").unwrap().result,
   346	        Ty::List(Box::new(Ty::Decimal(2)), 2));
   347	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "wide").unwrap().result, Ty::Decimal(12));
   348	    assert_eq!(bound.programs.iter().find(|p| p.program.name == "scaleZero").unwrap().result, Ty::Decimal(0));
   349	    let mut engine = Engine::memory(bound.schema, bound.programs.into_iter().map(|p| p.program)).unwrap();
   350	    let values = engine.query("rounded", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap().data;
   351	    assert_eq!(values, Value::Array([2, 3, 2, 3, 3, 2, 4, -3, -3, -2, -3, -2, 2, 3].into_iter().map(Value::Int).collect()));
   352	    for name in ["decimalValue", "moneyValue"] {
   353	        let value = engine.query(name, Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([("value".into(), Value::Int(5))]))).unwrap().data;
   354	        assert_eq!(value, Value::Int(2), "{name}");
   355	    }
   356	    let scaled = |engine: &mut Engine, numerator, denominator| engine.query("scaled", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
   357	        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(numerator)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(denominator)),
   358	    ]))).unwrap().data;
   359	    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(5050), Value::Int(5050)]));
   360	    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -101, 2), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-5050), Value::Int(-5050)]));
   361	    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, 1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(12), Value::Int(13)]));
   362	    assert_eq!(scaled(&mut engine, -1, 8), Value::Array(vec![Value::Int(-12), Value::Int(-13)]));
   363	    assert_eq!(engine.query("wide", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
   364	        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
   365	        ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX)),
   366	    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(1_000_000_000_000), "the wide scaled intermediate is not restricted to i53");
   367	    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaleZero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::from([
   368	        ("numerator".into(), Value::Int(5)), ("denominator".into(), Value::Int(2)),
   369	    ]))).unwrap().data, Value::Int(2));
   370	    assert_eq!(engine.query("scaledOverflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
   371	    assert_eq!(engine.query("zero", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_DIV_ZERO");
   372	
   373	    use snapback4_core::ir::{Builtin, Expr, Program, ProgramKind, Rounding, Stmt};
   374	    let overflow = Program {
   375	        name: "overflow".into(), kind: ProgramKind::Query, args: BTreeMap::new(),
   376	        read_time_granularity_ms: None, native: false, returned_shapes: BTreeMap::new(),
   377	        body: vec![Stmt::Return(Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Divide { rounding: Rounding::TowardZero, scale: None },
   378	            args: vec![Expr::Literal(Value::Int(i64::MIN)), Expr::Literal(Value::Int(-1))] })],
   379	    };
   380	    let mut raw = Engine::memory(Default::default(), [overflow]).unwrap();
   381	    assert_eq!(raw.query("overflow", Context::new("alice", BTreeMap::new())).unwrap_err().code, "E_OVERFLOW");
   382	
   383	    for bad in ["divide(1, 2, 'nearest')", "divide(1, 2, mode)", "divide(1, divisor, 'half-even')",
   384	        "divide(1, 2, 13, 'half-even')", "divide(1, 2, scale, 'half-even')"] {
   385	        let source = if bad.contains("mode") { format!("query bad(mode: enum('half-even')):\n  return {bad}\n") }
   386	            else if bad.contains("scale") { format!("query bad(scale: int):\n  return {bad}\n") }

   388	            else { format!("query bad():\n  return {bad}\n") };
   389	        let bound = compile(&[("bad.q".into(), source)]);
   390	        assert!(bound.diagnostics.iter().any(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE"), "{bad}: {:#?}", bound.diagnostics);
   391	    }

     4	impl<'a> Binder<'a> {
     5	    // @ref LLP 3000.011.000.001#4 — retain the binder's actual choice for why, never infer a new lookup or rewrite.
     6	    pub(super) fn record_selection(&mut self, site: &str, read: &ReadExpr, index: &ast::IndexDecl, result: &str, reason: &str) {
     7	        let named = read.keys.iter().all(|key| key.column.is_some());
     8	        let bindings = index.columns.iter().enumerate().filter_map(|(position, column)| {
     9	            let key = if named { read.keys.iter().find(|key| key.column.as_ref() == Some(column)) } else { read.keys.get(position) }?;
    10	            Some(format!("{column} = {}", self.catalog.source.operand(&key.value)))
    11	        }).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ");
    12	        let origin = if self.catalog.synthesized.contains(&(read.table.clone(), index.name.clone())) { "synthesized; " } else { "" };
    13	        let source = if origin.is_empty() { String::new() } else { format!("; read: {}", self.catalog.read_origins.get(&read.site.to_string()).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| print::read_expr(read))) };
    14	        let mut selection = format!("selected {} ({bindings}); result: {result}; {origin}{reason}{source}", index.name);
    15	        if !self.variants.is_empty() {
    16	            let when = self.variants.iter().map(|(name, present)| format!("{} {}", name.trim_start_matches("$intentPresent:").trim_start_matches("$intentSearch:"), if *present { "present" } else { "absent" })).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" and ");
    17	            selection = format!("when {when}: {selection}");
    18	        }
    19	        self.selections.entry(site.into()).and_modify(|prior| { if !prior.contains(&selection) { prior.push_str("; "); prior.push_str(&selection); } }).or_insert(selection);
    20	    }
    21	
    22	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#10 — a covered total unique key reads one row; additional named equalities check that row.
    23	    pub(super) fn read_value(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, mode: ReadMode, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<Expr> {
    24	        let info = self.table(&read.table, &read.site)?;
    25	        for key in &read.keys { if let Some(field) = &key.column { super::super::row_views::predicate_field(info, field, &read.site)?; } }
    26	        if !read.seeks.is_empty() { return Err(type_error(&read.site, "a seek needs a bounded page", "t[prefix, col >= start] first 50 by index")); }
    27	        let mut point = read.clone();
    28	        if point.keys.is_empty() && info.maintained.as_ref().is_some_and(|maintain| maintain.by.is_empty()) {
    29	            point.keys.push(ast::KeyPart { column: None, value: A::Literal { value: Literal::Bool(true), site: read.site.clone() }, site: read.site.clone() });
    30	            point.index = Some("byGroup".into());
    31	        } else if point.keys.is_empty() {
    32	            return Err(unknown(&read.site, format!("{}[] reads nothing; a point read needs a key", read.table), format!("{}[id]", read.table)));
    33	        }
    34	        let implicit_group = mode == ReadMode::FilteredPoint && info.maintained.is_some() && point.index.is_none();
    35	        if implicit_group { point.index = Some("byGroup".into()); }
    36	        let (mut keys, index, mut selection) = self.select_index(info, &point, mode, out)?;
    37	        super::super::point_key::check(info, &index, read, &keys.iter().map(|(column, _, ty)|
    38	            (column.as_deref(), !ty.is_optional() && *ty != Ty::Unknown)).collect::<Vec<_>>(), false)?;
    39	        if implicit_group { selection = "complete maintained group key".into(); }
    40	        let extra = keys.len() > index.columns.len();
    41	        let mut equalities = Vec::new();
    42	        if extra {
    43	            for (column, value, ty) in &mut keys {
    44	                let column = column.as_ref().expect("named key");
    45	                if column != "id" && !info.columns.contains_key(column) {
    46	                    return Err(unknown(&read.site, format!("{} has no column {column}", read.table), name_rewrite(column, info.columns.keys().map(String::as_str).chain(["id"]), None)));
    47	                }
    48	                let expected = self.key_ty(info, &index, column);
    49	                if !ty.comparable(&expected) { return Err(type_error(&read.site, format!("{column} is {}; {}.{column} is {}", ty.name(), read.table, expected.name()), format!("use {} for {column}", expected.name()))); }
    50	                *value = self.snapshot(value.clone(), out);
    51	                if !index.columns.contains(column) { equalities.push((column.clone(), value.clone())); }
    52	            }
    53	            keys.retain(|(column, _, _)| index.columns.contains(column.as_ref().unwrap()));
    54	        }
    55	        let key = self.order_keys(info, &index, keys)?;
    56	        let location = self.site();
    57	        self.record_selection(&location, read, &index, if mode == ReadMode::Exists { "exists" } else if info.maintained.is_some() { "scalar" } else { "row or null" }, &selection);
    58	        self.sources.insert(location.clone(), (read.site.clone(), print::read_expr(read)));
    59	        let mut point = Read { site: location, table: read.table.clone(), index: index.name, key, provenance: KeyProvenance::Shape };
    60	        // @ref LLP 3000.028#3.4 — only a caller-proved existence read may use the whole owner partition.
    61	        if mode == ReadMode::Exists && equalities.is_empty() {
    62	            super::super::own_keys::existence(self.schema, &mut point);
    63	        }
    64	        if equalities.is_empty() { return Ok(if mode == ReadMode::Exists { Expr::Exists(point) } else { Expr::Get(point) }); }
    65	        let row = self.temp("probe");
    66	        out.push(Stmt::Let { name: row.clone(), value: Expr::Get(point) });
    67	        let mut condition = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(ir::var(&row)), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) };
    68	        // @ref LLP 3000.014#5-what-derives-from-the-capture — a denied aggregate carries a null value, not a present group.
    69	        if mode == ReadMode::Exists && info.maintained.is_some() {
    70	            let present = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Ne, left: Box::new(ir::field(ir::var(&row), "value")), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Null)) };
    71	            condition = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::And, left: Box::new(condition), right: Box::new(present) };
    72	        }
    73	        for (column, value) in equalities {
    74	            let test = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Eq, left: Box::new(ir::field(ir::var(&row), &column)), right: Box::new(value) };
    75	            condition = Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::And, left: Box::new(condition), right: Box::new(test) };
    76	        }
    77	        if mode == ReadMode::Exists { return Ok(condition); }
    78	        out.push(Stmt::If { condition, then_body: Vec::new(), else_body: vec![Stmt::Assign { name: row.clone(), value: Expr::Literal(Value::Null) }] });
    79	        Ok(ir::var(&row))
    80	    }

    82	    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.3 — a seek constrains the first index column after the pinned prefix.
    83	    pub(super) fn seek(&mut self, info: &'a TableInfo, read: &ReadExpr, index: &ast::IndexDecl, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<Option<ir::Range>> {
    84	        if read.seeks.is_empty() { return Ok(None); }
    85	        let mut range = ir::Range { gt: None, gte: None, lt: None, lte: None };
    86	        for bound in &read.seeks {
    87	            if index.columns.get(read.keys.len()) != Some(&bound.column) || read.matching.is_some() {
    88	                return Err(type_error(&bound.site, "a seek compares the first unpinned column of a plain index", "t[prefix, col >= start, col < end] first 50 by index"));
    89	            }
    90	            let expected = self.key_ty(info, index, &bound.column);
    91	            let (value, ty) = self.field_value(&ObjectField { spread: false, name: bound.column.clone(), value: Some(bound.value.clone()), site: bound.site.clone() }, &expected, out)?;
    92	            if !ty.comparable(&expected) || ty.is_optional() {
    93	                let endpoint = print::expression(&bound.value);
    94	                let rewrite = if ty.is_optional() {
    95	                    format!("put the read inside `if {endpoint} != null:`, then `{} where .{} {} {endpoint}`", read.table, bound.column, bound.op)
    96	                } else {
    97	                    format!("use a present {} endpoint in `{} where .{} {} {endpoint}`", expected.required().name(), read.table, bound.column, bound.op)
    98	                };
    99	                return Err(type_error(&bound.site, format!("seek on {}.{} expects present {}, got {}", read.table, bound.column, expected.required().name(), ty.name()), rewrite));
   100	            }
   101	            let slot = match bound.op.as_str() { ">" => &mut range.gt, ">=" => &mut range.gte, "<" => &mut range.lt, "<=" => &mut range.lte, _ => unreachable!("parser seek comparison") };
   102	            if slot.is_some() { return Err(type_error(&bound.site, "a seek bound is repeated", "write one lower and one upper bound")); }
   103	            *slot = Some(Box::new(self.snapshot(value, out)));
   104	        }
   105	        if (range.gt.is_some() && range.gte.is_some()) || (range.lt.is_some() && range.lte.is_some()) {
   106	            return Err(type_error(&read.site, "a seek has at most one lower and one upper bound", "t[prefix, col >= start, col < end] first 50 by index"));
   107	        }
   108	        // Null sorts below every present value. An upper-only nullable seek
   109	        // must skip the entire null segment, including its id suffixes.
   110	        if range.gt.is_none() && range.gte.is_none()
   111	            && read.seeks.first().is_some_and(|bound| self.key_ty(info, index, &bound.column).is_optional()) {
   112	            range.gt = Some(Box::new(ir::lit(Value::Null)));
   113	        }
   114	        Ok(Some(range))
   115	    }
   116	}

   118	impl Binder<'_> {
   119	    pub(super) fn variant(&self) -> Option<ir::VariantId> {
   120	        (!self.variants.is_empty()).then(|| {
   121	            let hash = snapback4_core::value::digest(&self.variants);
   122	            std::array::from_fn(|i| u32::from_str_radix(&hash[i * 8..i * 8 + 8], 16).expect("hex digest"))
   123	        })
   124	    }

   128	        let predicate = read.filter.as_ref()?;
   129	        let (base, name, site) = trailing_shape(predicate)?;

   100	    pub(super) fn authorization_proved(&self, condition: &A, truth: bool) -> bool {

   108	            } if op == "and" && truth => {
   109	                self.authorization_proved(left, true) && self.authorization_proved(right, true)
   110	            }

   115	            }

   118	            } if op == "or" && truth => {

//! Expression lowering with branch-owned setup statements.

use super::*;
use snapback4_core::calendar::Civil;

impl Binder<'_> {
    /// Bare tables are domains only at an aggregate/loop consumer; ordinary
    /// names keep their lexical meaning and ordinary pages keep their bounds.
    pub(super) fn aggregate_domain(&self, value: &A) -> Option<ReadExpr> {
        match value {
            A::Read(read) if read.range.is_none() && read.matching.is_none() => Some(read.clone()),
            A::Name { name, site } if self.binding(name).is_none() && self.catalog.tables.contains_key(name) =>
                Some(ReadExpr { cursor_prefix: None, order_keys: Vec::new(), computed: Default::default(), table: name.clone(), keys: Vec::new(), index: Some("byId".into()), range: None, matching: None, filter: None, seeks: Vec::new(), site: site.clone() }),
            _ => None,
        }
    }

    // ----- expressions -----

    /// An expression whose value is used (bound, returned, or a final
    /// write): writes yield their row.
    pub(super) fn value_of(&mut self, value: &A, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if let A::Write { .. } = value {
            return self.write(value, out, true).map(|opt| opt.expect("a valued write"));
        }
        self.expr(value, out)
    }

    /// Strict compound children run in source order, before setup emitted by
    /// a later child. Lexical values and their fields cannot change here;
    /// leaving those fields in their object also preserves pending provenance.
    pub(super) fn snapshot(&mut self, value: Expr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Expr {
        if matches!(value, Expr::Literal(_) | Expr::Input(Input::Viewer | Input::Now)) || lexical_value(&value) {
            return value;
        }
        let name = self.temp("value");
        out.push(Stmt::Let { name: name.clone(), value });
        ir::var(&name)
    }

    pub(super) fn sequence_setup<'e>(&mut self, prior: impl Iterator<Item = &'e mut Expr>, setup: setup::Body, out: &mut setup::Body) {
        if !setup.is_empty() {
            for value in prior {
                *value = self.snapshot(std::mem::replace(value, Expr::Literal(Value::Null)), out);
            }
            out.extend(setup);
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn strict_args(&mut self, args: &[A], out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<Vec<(Expr, Ty)>> {
        let mut values = Vec::<(Expr, Ty)>::new();
        let mut failed = None;
        for arg in args {
            let mut setup = setup::Body::default();
            match self.expr(arg, &mut setup) {
                Ok(value) => {
                    self.sequence_setup(values.iter_mut().map(|(e, _)| e), setup, out);
                    values.push(value);
                }
                Err(error) => { self.record_error(error.clone()); failed.get_or_insert(error); }
            }
        }
        match failed { Some(error) => Err(error), None => Ok(values) }
    }

    pub(super) fn expr(&mut self, expr: &A, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        // Only shape/object/list construction forwards output position. Every
        // operator, call, key, predicate and assertion consumes its operands.
        let prior = self.returned_data;
        self.returned_data &= matches!(expr, A::Array { .. } | A::Object { .. } | A::Shape { .. } | A::ShapeUse { .. } | A::Member { .. } | A::Name { .. } | A::Focal { .. });
        let start = out.len();
        let result = self.expr_inner(expr, out);
        if !matches!(expr, A::Write { .. }) && point_facts::writes(&out[start..]) { self.invalidate_points(); }
        self.returned_data = prior;
        // Even a builtin's ordinary type refusal should explain why a whole
        // maintained value cannot be consumed. Successful calls are checked by
        // the shared IR allowlist; this only improves already-failing calls.
        if result.as_ref().is_err_and(|d| d.code == "E_QUARRY_TYPE") {
            let args: Vec<&A> = match expr { A::Call { args, .. } => args.iter().collect(), A::Binary { left, right, .. } => vec![left, right], _ => vec![] };
            let mut probe = self.clone();
            for arg in args {
                if let Ok((_, ty)) = probe.expr(arg, &mut setup::Body::default()) {
                    self.maintenance_operand(&ty, arg.site())?;
                }
            }
        }
        let result = result?;
        if !self.schema.receipts.is_empty() {
            let site = self.call_chain.iter().find(|(name, _)| self.catalog.documents.iter().flat_map(|d| &d.tables).filter_map(|t| t.receipts.as_ref()).any(|clause| &clause.operations[0] == name))
                .map(|(_, site)| site).unwrap_or_else(|| expr.site());
    }

    pub(super) fn check_meter_prefix(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, scan: &Scan, aggregate: bool) -> Fallible<()> {
        if scan.take != Bound::Meter || snapback4_core::engine::rules::scan_visibility(self.schema, scan).uniform { return Ok(()); }
        let table = &self.schema.tables[&scan.table];
        let index = &table.indexes[&scan.index];
        let pinned = index.columns().into_iter().take(scan.prefix.len()).collect::<std::collections::BTreeSet<_>>();
        let used = snapback4_core::engine::rules::deciding_fields(&scan.table, table, &table.rules.read);
        let missing = used.difference(&pinned).cloned().collect::<Vec<_>>();
        let mut leading = missing.clone();
        for column in index.columns().into_iter().skip(scan.prefix.len()) { if !leading.contains(&column) { leading.push(column); } }
        let mut page = read.clone();
        page.range = Some(ast::RangeSpec { order: ast::Order::Asc, take: 50, cursor: Some(Box::new(A::Name { name: "c".into(), site: read.site.clone() })), site: read.site.clone() });
        // @ref LLP 3000.028#4-put-the-rules-where-the-builder-meets-them — preserve the loop, callers and truncation cost in the reason.
        let jobs = self.call_chain.last().filter(|_| self.call_chain.len() > 1)
            .map(|(helper, _)| self.helper_job_callers(helper)).unwrap_or_default();
        let query_site = &self.call_chain[0].1;
        let declaration = self.catalog.source.declarations.get(&query_site.to_string());
        if aggregate && (self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query || jobs.is_empty() || declaration.is_none()) {
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#11 — a total has no first-N repair (app-farm lane 087).
            let deciding = if missing.is_empty() { leading.join(", ") } else { missing.iter().map(|c| format!(".{c}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", ") };
            let grant = snapback4_core::engine::rules::grant_decision(self.schema, scan);
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#17.8 — a readable grant the program requires before the total (`require exists staff[viewer]`)
            // makes every row readable for every caller who reaches it, which the server decides once (read.rs `granted`).
            let guard = grant.as_ref().map_or_else(String::new, |grant| format!("; or guard it with the grant, so every caller who reaches it reads every row: `require {} else …` before it (or `if {}:` around it)", grant.quarry(), grant.quarry()));
            let diagnostic = Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", format!("{} by {}: a total over rows the viewer may only partly read is not decided by its pinned columns, so no page bound makes it exact", scan.table, scan.index),
                format!("pin {deciding} with where equalities so one verdict covers every row (the total then covers only that scope){guard}; {}. If the maintained count keeps the source's private read rule, its group keys must carry every field that rule reads (including {deciding}); a public total instead deliberately discloses the count across hidden rows; or return a `first N` page with a cursor and fold it in the client", self.total_view_recipe(read, scan))).guide("bounds");
            if grant.is_some() && self.caller_kind == ProgramKind::Query && self.call_chain.len() == 1 {
                self.pending_totals.push((scan.site.clone(), diagnostic));
                return Ok(());
            }
            return Err(diagnostic);
        }
        if self.caller_kind != ProgramKind::Query || jobs.is_empty() || declaration.is_none() {
            return Err(Diagnostic::new(&read.site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", format!("{} by {}: a meter-bounded prefix needs a read rule uniformly decided by its pinned columns", scan.table, scan.index),
                format!("use `first N`: `{}` (declare `c: cursor ?` and follow its cursor); for a complete read, scan by an index leading with {} and pin the deciding columns (N_NEVER_COMPLETE)", self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(page)), leading.join(", "))).guide("bounds"));
        }
        let chain = self.call_chain.iter().map(|(name, site)| format!("{name} (at {site})")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(" -> ");
        let job = format!("the system job caller(s) {}", jobs.join(", "));
        let authored = self.catalog.read_origins.get(&read.site.to_string()).cloned().unwrap_or_else(|| self.catalog.source.expression(&A::Read(read.clone())));
        let rule = if missing.is_empty() { "read rule".into() } else { format!("{}-based read rule", missing.join(", ")) };
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#23 — a whole-query replacement points to that declaration, never its shared helper.
        let end = query_site.line + declaration.unwrap().lines().count() as u32 - 1;
        let context = format!("; viewer query caller chain: {chain}. `{authored}` (at {}) does not decide its {rule}; a helper grants no system authority. The replacement is for the entire unused viewer query `{}`: replace lines {}-{end} in {} with the printed comment. Keep the complete scheduled job. A separately named paged preview needs its own cursor; `first 50` is a partial preview, not an equivalent complete total. For a complete per-group read, pin {}. Inner recipient work must fit one chunk even when the outer sweep adapts its chunk size; an oversized recipient parks with E_BOUND rather than committing a partial total", read.site, self.call_chain[0].0, query_site.line, query_site.file, leading.join(", "));
        Err(Diagnostic::new(query_site, "E_QUARRY_BOUND", format!("{} by {}: a meter-bounded prefix needs a read rule uniformly decided by its pinned columns{context}", scan.table, scan.index),
            format!("-- {} removed: keep the complete helper under {job}'s chunk meter.", self.call_chain[0].0)).guide("bounds"))
    }

    /// A maintained view that keeps this total, rendered from the author's own
    /// table, column and group (lanes 007 062 067: "hard to map to this schema").
    // @ref LLP 3000.036#13.10 — a total over partly readable rows: the view discloses the total, never the rows.
    fn total_view_recipe(&self, read: &ReadExpr, scan: &Scan) -> String {
        use crate::bind::intent::{column, split};
        let table = &scan.table;
        let (kind, of) = self.total.clone().unwrap_or(("count", None));
        // The group: the read's equalities, in its index order.
        let mut groups: Vec<(String, String)> = read.keys.iter().filter_map(|key| key.column.clone().map(|column| (column, print::expression(&key.value)))).collect();
        let mut filters = Vec::new();
        if let Some(filter) = read.filter.clone() { split(*filter, &mut filters); }
        for filter in &filters {
            if let A::Binary { op, left, right, .. } = filter && op == "=" && let Some(col) = column(left)
                && super::super::intent::independent(right) && !groups.iter().any(|(c, _)| c == col) {
                groups.push((col.to_owned(), print::expression(right)));
            }
        }
        let suffix = if kind == "count" { "Count" } else { "Total" };
        let name = format!("{table}{suffix}");
        let aggregate = match &of { Some(column) => format!("sum {table} of {column}"), None => format!("count {table}") };
        let (readers, who) = match snapback4_core::engine::rules::grant_decision(self.schema, scan) {
            Some(grant) => (grant.quarry(), "the callers that grant admits"),
            None => ("allow".to_owned(), "everyone; narrow it to the readers the total is for"),
        };
        if groups.is_empty() {
            // @ref LLP 3000.036#17.2 — a view needs a group key (the core refuses an empty `by`): a whole-table
            // total groups by a column every row holds the same value of (lane 020 pasted `count t` and got E_QUARRY_SYNTAX).
            let key = (1..).map(|n| if n == 1 { "totalKey".to_owned() } else { format!("totalKey{n}") })
                .find(|key| !table_columns(self.schema, table).contains(key)).unwrap();
            return format!("or keep the total in a view, which discloses the total, never the rows; a view groups by a key, so give every {table} row the same one: add `{key}: enum('all') default 'all'` and `immutable {key}` to {table}, declare `view {name}: {aggregate} by .{key}` with `read <- {readers}` ({who}), then read `{name}['all']`");
        }
        let by = format!(" by {}", groups.iter().map(|(c, _)| format!(".{c}")).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
        let lookup = format!("{name}[{}]", groups.iter().map(|(_, v)| v.clone()).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(", "));
        format!("or keep the total in a view, which discloses the total, never the rows: `view {name}: {aggregate}{by}` with `read <- {readers}` ({who}), then read `{lookup}`")
    }

    // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.22 — ruling 25: program existence over a prefix is a top-1 scan below page ownership; rule probes retain their exact-key path.
    pub(super) fn exists_read(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        self.exists_probe(read, out).map_err(|error| super::super::bracket_ranges::refusal(read, false, error))
    }

    fn exists_probe(&mut self, read: &ReadExpr, out: &mut setup::Body) -> Fallible<(Expr, Ty)> {
        if !self.is_page(read, ReadMode::Exists)? { return Ok((self.read_value(read, ReadMode::Exists, out)?, Ty::Bool)); }
        let (scan, _) = self.scan_at(read, out, Position::Exists)?;
        Ok((Expr::Binary { op: BinaryOp::Gt, left: Box::new(Expr::Builtin { builtin: Builtin::Count, args: vec![Expr::Scan(scan)] }), right: Box::new(Expr::Literal(Value::Int(0))) }, Ty::Bool))
    }
}

fn table_columns(schema: &snapback4_core::schema::Schema, table: &str) -> Vec<String> {
    schema.table(table).map(|t| t.columns.keys().cloned().collect()).unwrap_or_default()
}

# Wave 12 language-lane status

Updated: 2026-10-15

## Scope

This lane owns the five semantic gaps: ungrouped maintained totals, sound
aggregate and maintained-result narrowing, email text format, enum search,
and exact rounded decimal division. It does not own engine expiry,
`maintained_id`, parser recovery, reserved-name diagnostics or the branch
planner.

## Progress

- Governing LLPs, guide cards, wave evidence lanes 019/021/027/083/091/093,
  NA10 and the pattern ledger read.
- Baseline gate `/tmp/lang-baseline-ready` observed before production edits.
- LLP 3000.013.001 records the semantic and verification contract and is
  linked into `llp/current/`.
- Email schema/runtime/client support landed in `b081f96054`.
- The remaining semantic foundation landed in `0fe7cc1263`: ungrouped global
  maintained counts, enum search, exact three/four-argument rounded division,
  and capture-time count provenance with stale-proof invalidation.
- Cross-runtime evidence landed in `4156cdf7e5`: generated rounded-division
  cases cover every mode/scale and compile into the Lean fragment; one drawn
  representative executes through native, Lean and both device stores. Simulator and
  device scenarios exercise all five surfaces; standalone Lean witnesses
  cover the semantic fragments outside the row evaluator.
- The shared Lean lowering compile blocker reported in the coordination inbox
  is repaired; both Wave 12 language test executables compile again.
- Affected language tests pass 6/6. Simulator, difftest generation, memory
  device and SQLite device tests pass 1/1 each. Lean passes 54 build jobs, 65
  audited theorems, 88/88 examples and 7/7 fixtures. The focused CLI guide
  lookup regression passes, and `ref-check --verbose` passes.
- The full guide test currently passes 120/123. Its three residual failures
  are in concurrent, uncommitted diagnostics documentation: the maintained
  disclosure example names an undeclared table and exceeds its card budget,
  a personas block duplicates the project identity declaration, and their
  added prose moves the corpus-wide reduction ratio. Wave 12's modified guide
  examples, compiled-block preservation, language execution and email
  expectation all pass in that same run.
- Guide/spec commit and the two fresh blind READY reviews are in progress.

## Concerns / decisions

- Count non-emptiness is an exact transaction fact, never a general theorem
  prover; conservative misses are acceptable, stale acceptance is not.
- The intermediate census's owner-or-manager structural-fanout refusals are
  in the planner/diagnostics lanes: this lane does not change OR-role planning.
- Hidden maintained misses remain null. Zero is produced only after an
  authorization proof.
- Rounded division uses exact signed integer quotient/remainder and an
  explicit enum mode. The four-argument integer form also names result scale,
  so fractional averages need no manual fixed-point multiply; no floating
  point or implicit `avg` is introduced.

+/// Exact rounded division comes from its own stream, preserving every older
+/// case whose stream does not select the new expression.
+fn rounded_division(case: &mut Case) {
+    let mut rng = Rng::new(case.seed ^ ROUND_DIV_STREAM);
+    if rng.pick(6) != 0 || !matches!(case.program.body, Body::Scalar(_)) { return; }
+    let modes = [Rounding::TowardZero, Rounding::AwayFromZero, Rounding::Floor,
+        Rounding::Ceiling, Rounding::HalfAwayFromZero, Rounding::HalfEven];
+    let dividend = if rng.pick(2) == 0 { Expr::Arg("a".into(), Type::Int) }
+        else { Expr::Int([-7, -5, -1, 0, 1, 5, 7][rng.pick(7) as usize]) };
+    let divisor = if rng.pick(2) == 0 { Expr::Arg("b".into(), Type::Int) }
+        else { Expr::Int([-3, -2, -1, 0, 1, 2, 3][rng.pick(7) as usize]) };
+    let scale = match rng.pick(5) { 0 => None, 1 => Some(0), 2 => Some(2), 3 => Some(6), _ => Some(12) };
+    case.program.body = Body::Scalar(Expr::RoundedDivide(
+        modes[rng.pick(modes.len() as u64) as usize].clone(), scale, Box::new(dividend), Box::new(divisor)));

     2	// @ref LLP 3000.015#1 — raw blob lengths never enter a principal's meter.
     3	use super::*;
     4	use crate::schema::ColumnType;
     5	
     6	/// Includes serialized storage scratch, typed decode, escaping scratch, map
     7	/// nodes and geometric array growth. Id/Principal/Ref have the admission bound
     8	/// of 144 canonical tagged bytes (value::validate_identities), on every host.
     9	pub fn actual_size(table: &Table) -> bool {
    10	    // A read-through child inherits its parent's rule and lifetime; it is never public.
    11	    table.rules.read.is_uniformly_readable() && !table.read_lifetime_sensitive() && table.through.is_none()
    12	        && table.recorded.is_empty() && table.written_by.values().all(|a| a.audience)
    13	}
    14	
    15	/// Public images use the metered store adapter; private images reserve before decode.
    16	pub fn admission(table: &Table) -> u64 {
    17	    if actual_size(table) { 0 } else { decode_reservation(table) }
    18	}
    19	
    20	pub fn decode_reservation(table: &Table) -> u64 {
    21	    table.columns.iter().fold(4096 + MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES as u64 * 4, |n, (name, ty)| {
    22	            n.saturating_add(256 + name.len() as u64 * 16).saturating_add(column(ty))
    23	        })
    24	}
    25	
    26	fn column(ty: &ColumnType) -> u64 {
    27	    use ColumnType::*;
    28	    match ty {
    29	        Id | Principal | Ref { .. } => 144 * 16,
    30	        Text { max } => u64::from(*max) * 16,
    31	        Bytes { max } => u64::from(*max) * 16,
    32	        Enum { variants } => variants.iter().map(|v| v.len() as u64 * 16).max().unwrap_or(0),
    33	        Optional(inner) => column(inner),
    34	        List { of, max } | ListRange { of, max, .. } => u64::from(*max).saturating_mul(256_u64.saturating_add(column(of))).saturating_add(256),
    35	        Json { max_bytes } => u64::from(*max_bytes) * 256,
    36	        Image { .. } | Video { .. } | File { .. } => 16384, // bounded asset facts, never file bytes
    37	        Int | IntRange { .. } | Decimal { .. } | Money { .. } | Bool | Time => 256,
    38	    }
    39	}

   129	    match remaining with
   130	    | [] => (if current.isEmpty then tokens else current.reverse :: tokens).reverse
   131	    | c :: cs =>
   132	        if asciiAlphaNum c then go cs (asciiLower c :: current) tokens
   133	        else go cs [] (if current.isEmpty then tokens else current.reverse :: tokens)

   137	  | [], _ => true
   138	  | _, [] => false
   139	  | p :: ps, w :: ws => p == w && isPrefix ps ws

   141	def enumMatchesAscii (value query : String) : Bool :=
   142	  let words := asciiTokens value
   143	  (asciiTokens query).all fun term => words.any fun word => isPrefix term word

   147	example : enumMatchesAscii "museum" "music" = false := by decide

  `{"arr":[…]}` and `{"row":[[name, value], …]}` (ordered pairs).
- **Rules, terms, expressions, statements and writes** use one key per
  constructor of `Syntax.lean`, with the constructor's arguments
  (`CaseJson.lean` is the decoder). `"viewer"`, `"allow"` and `"deny"` are
  bare strings.
- **Store rows** are `{"id":…,"cols":{name: scalar}}`; columns are put in the
  table's declared order and an absent column is null.
- **Lower read lifetimes** use a table's optional `notBefore` column and the
  case's integer `now`. Null and values at or before `now` are open. The model
  filters the whole logical view, including rule probes and write-result
  visibility, while write target resolution and constraints remain physical.
  Generated model cases seed at this one request clock; bounded publication
  of an existing due-row backlog is a runtime/device lifecycle concern.
- **The output** is one of:
  - `{"kind":"answer","data":…,"complete":b,"next":…}`;
  - `{"kind":"unavailable"}`;
  - `{"kind":"refused","code":"…"}`;
  - `{"kind":"committed","result":…,"store":{…}}` (the store in the input's
    row form, so a follow-up case can run over it);
  - `{"kind":"error","error":"…"}` for a line that does not decode. The
    harness treats it as an emitter defect, never as a verdict.

  Every value is tagged. (`Outcome.toJson` in `Json.lean`, used by the
  examples, still prints ids and text alike, as on the wire.)

How the harness compares against the engine's outcome record:

| Model | Engine field | Rule |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `kind` | refusal / `unavailable` / data / committed | exact |
| `refused.code` | `refusal.code` (or a failed write's `why.code`) | exact; sites are not modelled |
| `answer.data`, `committed.result` | `data`, `result` | exact, both tagged; rows compare as field maps |
| `answer.complete` | `complete` | exact |
| `answer.next` | `next` | presence only (OPEN C1); then each side continues from its own cursor and the next page is compared, to the end |
| `committed.store` | the engine's store | through `observe` (a point reread), run on each side's resulting store |
| (none) | meter fields, cut sites, `tables`, `seq` | not compared: out of scope; explicit expiry sweeps advance and compare both stores |

The engine runs at the default ceilings and the model unbounded, so no
compared case is cut. Comparing cuts (OPEN M1: a cut is reported, and
continuation reaches the uncut answer, `cut_continuation`) is not yet done.

//! Conservative control outcomes, composed in execution order.
use super::{Expr, Stmt, Value};

const FALLS_THROUGH: u8 = 1;
const BREAKS: u8 = 2;
const CONTINUES: u8 = 4;
// A refusal, like a return, cannot reach any later use of a local.
const RETURNS: u8 = 8;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(super) struct Outcomes(u8);

impl Outcomes {
    // @ref LLP 3000.007#5.1 — loop transfers carry local types; later statements cannot erase those paths.
    pub(super) fn block(statements: &[Stmt]) -> Self {
        let mut outcomes = FALLS_THROUGH;
        for statement in statements {
            if outcomes & FALLS_THROUGH == 0 { break; }
            // Only paths still falling through execute the next statement.
            outcomes = (outcomes & !FALLS_THROUGH) | Self::statement(statement);
        }
        Self(outcomes)
    }

    fn statement(statement: &Stmt) -> u8 {
        match statement {
            Stmt::Return(_) => RETURNS,
            Stmt::Break => BREAKS,
            Stmt::Continue => CONTINUES,
            Stmt::Require { condition: Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(false)), .. } => RETURNS,
            Stmt::Require { .. } => FALLS_THROUGH | RETURNS,
            Stmt::If { then_body, else_body, .. } => Self::block(then_body).0 | Self::block(else_body).0,
            // The loop may be empty or finish. Its own break/continue paths
            // do not transfer out of the enclosing loop; returns still do.
            Stmt::For { body, .. } => FALLS_THROUGH | (Self::block(body).0 & RETURNS),
            Stmt::Const { .. } | Stmt::Let { .. } | Stmt::Assign { .. }
            | Stmt::Push { .. } | Stmt::Check { .. } | Stmt::InsertIfAbsent { .. }
            | Stmt::Insert { .. } | Stmt::Update { .. } | Stmt::Upsert { .. }
            | Stmt::WriteTarget { .. } | Stmt::DeleteTarget { .. } | Stmt::Delete { .. } | Stmt::Emit { .. } => FALLS_THROUGH,
        }
    }

    pub(super) fn exits(self) -> bool { self.0 & FALLS_THROUGH == 0 }
    pub(super) fn falls_through(self) -> bool { self.0 & FALLS_THROUGH != 0 }
    pub(super) fn terminates(self) -> bool { self.0 == RETURNS }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::bind::program::LoopDomain;

    fn returned() -> Stmt { Stmt::Return(Expr::Literal(Value::Int(0))) }
    fn refused() -> Stmt {
        Stmt::Require { condition: Expr::Literal(Value::Bool(false)), code: "STOP".into(), site: None, message: None }
    }
    fn maybe(body: Vec<Stmt>) -> Stmt {
        Stmt::If { condition: Expr::Variable("stop".into()), then_body: body, else_body: vec![] }
    }
    fn looped(body: Vec<Stmt>) -> Stmt {
        Stmt::For { binding: "n".into(), domain: LoopDomain::LiteralRange { start: 0, end_exclusive: 2 }, body }
    }

    #[test]
    fn transfers_and_termination_keep_their_statement_order() {
        for (transfer, bit) in [(Stmt::Break, BREAKS), (Stmt::Continue, CONTINUES)] {
            for end in [returned(), refused()] {
                assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[transfer.clone(), end.clone()]), Outcomes(bit));
                assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[end.clone(), transfer.clone()]), Outcomes(RETURNS));
                let mixed = Outcomes::block(&[maybe(vec![transfer.clone()]), end.clone()]);
                assert_eq!(mixed, Outcomes(bit | RETURNS));
                assert!(mixed.exits());
                assert!(!mixed.terminates());
                assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[maybe(vec![end]), transfer.clone()]), mixed);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_falling_paths_reach_later_statements_and_loops_own_their_transfers() {
        assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[]), Outcomes(FALLS_THROUGH));
        assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[maybe(vec![returned()])]), Outcomes(FALLS_THROUGH | RETURNS));
        let both = Stmt::If { condition: Expr::Variable("ready".into()), then_body: vec![returned()], else_body: vec![refused()] };
        assert!(Outcomes::block(&[both, Stmt::Continue]).terminates());
        for body in [vec![], vec![Stmt::Break], vec![Stmt::Continue]] {
            assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[looped(body.clone())]), Outcomes(FALLS_THROUGH));
            assert!(Outcomes::block(&[looped(body), returned()]).terminates());
        }
        assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[looped(vec![returned()])]), Outcomes(FALLS_THROUGH | RETURNS));
        let nested = looped(vec![looped(vec![Stmt::Break]), Stmt::Continue]);
        assert_eq!(Outcomes::block(&[nested, Stmt::Break]), Outcomes(BREAKS));
    }
}

# Totals: count and sum in queries, mutations, jobs and views

Count rows or add up a column with `count` and `sum` inside a query, mutation or job. A view keeps a total per group current on every write, so reading it costs one row.

```quarry
table orders:
  owner: principal
  status: text <=10
  cents: int
  at: time default now
  immutable owner, at
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  update <- deny
  delete <- deny
  online only
view spentByOwner: sum orders of .cents by .owner
  online only
view spentPerDay: sum orders of .cents by .owner, day(.at)
  online only

query myTotals(since: time):
  open = count(orders where .owner = viewer and .status = 'open')
  recent = sum(orders where .owner = viewer and .at >= since, .cents)
  return { open, recent, lifetime: spentByOwner[viewer], today: spentPerDay[viewer, day(now)], yesterday: spentPerDay[viewer, day(now) - 1] }
```

There are two spellings, and they do not mix:

- **Inside an operation** (query, mutation, job): `count(t where …)` and
  `sum(t where …, .col)`. The parentheses are required; the column is the
  second argument, written `.col`. `min` and `max` take the same arguments.
- **In a view** (declared at top level): `view name: count t by .key` or
  `view name: sum t of .col by .key`, optionally `where …` before `by`
  (`sum t of .col where … by .key`, in that order). Read
  it by its group key, `spentByOwner[viewer]`; a group with no rows reads `0`.
  Omit `by` for one global scalar, `view orderCount: count orders`, and read it
  as `orderCount`. Its authorized empty value is `0` even though zero has no
  physical aggregate row.
  A view over an `online only` table is read online; its own `online only`
  line is optional.

## In a job

A job's totals are ordinary domain reads inside its sweep; write them where a
screen can read them:

```quarry
table readings:
  owner: principal
  value: int
  at: time default now
  immutable owner, at
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  update <- deny
  delete <- deny
  online only
table sensors:
  owner: principal
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  update <- deny
  delete <- deny
  online only
table dailyStats:
  owner: principal
  day: time
  n: int
  total: int
  read <- .owner = viewer
  insert <- deny
  update <- deny
  delete <- deny
  online only

job dailyTotals(periodStart: time, periodEnd: time):
  for s in sensors by .id:
    n = count(readings where .owner = s.owner and .at >= periodStart and .at < periodEnd)
    total = sum(readings where .owner = s.owner and .at >= periodStart and .at < periodEnd, .value)
    insert dailyStats { owner: s.owner, day: periodStart, n, total }
schedule nightly every 1d at 00:05: dailyTotals
```

`periodStart` and `periodEnd` are the schedule's period, so each run totals
one day. When the job only needs a number a screen shows, a view is usually
simpler than a job: `view perDay: sum readings of .value by .owner, day(.at)`
read as `perDay[viewer, day(now)]`.

## Rows the caller partly reads

An inline total counts only what its caller may read, so `check` refuses one
whose read rule its pins do not decide (`E_QUARRY_BOUND`, or
`E_STRUCTURAL_FANOUT` in a mutation): it would be a different number for
each caller, and a capacity check would miss hidden rows. Three exact forms:
pin the deciding column (`.owner = viewer`: the caller's own total); or keep
the total in a view whose read rule names who sees it (the view discloses the
total, never the rows); or, in a mutation, `require` below a view's count.

```quarry
table staff:
  principal: principal
  role: text <=20
  unique principal
  read <- .principal = viewer
  online only
table requests:
  owner: principal
  dept: text <=20
  amount: money USD
  read <- .owner = viewer or exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
  insert <- .owner = viewer
  online only
view requestsTotal: sum requests of .amount by .dept
  read <- exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
view requestsByOwner: sum requests of .amount by .owner, .dept
  read <- .owner = viewer

query deptTotal(dept: text <=20):
  return requestsTotal[dept] ! else NOT_ALLOWED
query myDeptTotal(dept: text <=20):
  return requestsByOwner[viewer, dept]
```

Finance reads every department's total; each requester reads their own.
`E_QUARRY_BOUND`'s rewrite prints this view for your table, column and group.
A keyed private view stays nullable until its own read rule is proved. For
example, after `require exists staff[principal = viewer, role = 'finance']
else NOT_FINANCE`, `requestsTotal[dept] + 1` is well typed and a readable
missing group contributes zero. A hidden stored group and a hidden miss both
remain null. A following write or viewer change invalidates the proof before
another keyed read.
A view may omit `by` for a whole-table scalar: `view requestsCount: count
requests`, read as bare `requestsCount`. The scalar still obeys its view read
rule: an authorized absence is zero, while a hidden stored or absent value is
null. Keep a real group key when callers need independent totals.
A guard on the read rule's own grant admits an inline total, as it admits a
staff page (`guide indexes`): after `require exists staff[principal = viewer,
role = 'finance'] else …` (or inside `if` on it), `sum(requests, .amount)` is
every row's total, because every caller who reaches it reads every row. A guard
on any other role does not; use the view.

For extrema over a domain, first establish that exact domain is non-empty:
`n = count(orders where .owner = viewer)` followed by `require n > 0 else
EMPTY`. From there, `min` and `max` of a required column on the identical
domain are required values; `sum` already has a zero identity. Optional projected columns remain optional. A
write, local rebinding, viewer/authority scope change, or different key/filter
invalidates the proof.

## Choosing

- A total a screen shows on every visit: a view. It is maintained on each
  write and read by key, constant work regardless of history.
- A rolling window (last 7 days): bucket the view by `day(.at)` (or
  `hour(.at)`, `bucket(.at, 15m)`) and add the buckets you need with point
  reads, `perDay[viewer, day(now)] + perDay[viewer, day(now) - 1]`.
- A one-off or filtered total (since an argument, by status): `count(...)` or
  `sum(...)` in the operation. It streams the domain under the meter: each
  row is authorized, filtered, folded and released. Its work grows with the
  matching rows, and `check --cost` says so; bound the predicate by an indexed
  time or a group key.
- `count(page)` and `sum(page, .col)` over a page you already read count only
  that page, not the population.

## Details

A meter cut never yields a partial total: the read is unavailable (the client
shows `loading`), including before `??`. On a device, an inline total needs
the device to hold its whole domain; otherwise the observation stays
`loading`, never a partial total. Sums take `int`, `decimal` or `money` columns; a total
that overflows refuses the transaction. `guide maintains` has every view form
(filters, reference paths, time buckets, offsets and sync); `guide reads`
covers totals beside pages and `exists`; `guide jobs` the sweep a job's totals
live in.

Common misspellings and what `check` says:

- `sum(orders of .cents)` (the view spelling inside an operation):
  `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown shape of`. Write `sum(orders where …, .cents)`.
- `count orders where .owner = viewer` without parentheses:
  `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown shape where`. Write `count(orders where …)`.
- `sum(orders where …, cents)`: `E_QUARRY_UNKNOWN: unknown name cents`. The
  column is `.cents`.

Reference-grouped views over `read through .parent` rows inherit the parent's
rule. Omit a read line that repeats `.parent.owner = viewer`; it is
`E_REDUNDANT_RULE`, and deleting the whole line preserves the inherited audience.
Maintained sums spell the value separately: `view total: sum expenses of .amount by .household`,
not `sum expenses.amount by .household`.
18-Reference contexts project required rows’ `.id`. Media: decimal KB/MB/GB.

20-Columns/arguments become nullable with `?`; omission becomes null. Table types are references; neither typing nor membership reads the target: use `require exists t[id] else CODE` or `r = t[id] ! else CODE`.
21:Defaults fill omissions; explicit values win. Formats: handle/url/email. `format email` is the shared ASCII address contract described below; identity providers may apply additional policy.
22:Money/decimal are scaled integers; fractions refuse E_INPUT. Divide them by an int with an explicit rounding mode, for example `divide(amount, 3, 'half-even')`. To produce a fractional decimal from integer inputs, name its result scale: `divide(total, count, 2, 'half-even')` returns `decimal 2`; no floating point or manual `total * 100` is introduced. Identical admitted unique-key reads narrow after exists/non-null guards, including pure helper arguments; writes, rebinding and viewer changes invalidate proof. A matching positive `count(domain)` guard also makes `min` and `max` of a required column non-null until a write or authority change invalidates that proof; `sum` already has a zero identity.

25-
26-- Guard or assert nullable values before passing them to required parameters: E_QUARRY_TYPE.
27-- Values and arithmetic must fit the integer range: E_OVERFLOW.
28-- `/` and `%` take ints and floor: `-7 / 2` is -4, `-7 % 2` is 1. A divisor must be nonzero: E_DIV_ZERO.
29:- `divide(value, int, mode)` preserves int/decimal/money and requires one of `toward-zero`, `away-from-zero`, `floor`, `ceiling`, `half-away-from-zero` or `half-even` as a literal mode. It uses checked integer quotient/remainder arithmetic; zero refuses E_DIV_ZERO and overflow refuses E_OVERFLOW.
30:- `divide(int, int, scale, mode)` returns `decimal scale`; `scale` is a literal from 0 through 12. Scaling uses a checked wide integer, then applies the same signed rounding rule and i53 result check. Null inputs are never zero.
31-- New required defaults must also fit the existing store: E_ADOPT.

     2	use super::{runner::Runner, write_target::row_copy_ceiling};
     3	use crate::{

    11	    // @ref LLP 3000.014#5-what-derives-from-the-capture — a point hit, miss or denial reserves the same reusable row scratch before discovering occupancy.
    12	    pub(super) fn aggregate_point_scratch(&self, maintain: &Maintain, key: &[Value]) -> u64 {
    13	        let source = &self.schema.tables[&maintain.source];
    14	        row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[&maintain.target])
    15	            .saturating_mul(17)
    16	            .saturating_add(
    17	                // The key is the caller's evaluated input, never a stored image.
    18	                key.iter()
    19	                    .map(|value| match value { Value::String(s) | Value::Id(s) => s.len() as u64, Value::Bytes(b) => b.len() as u64, _ => 0 })
    20	                    .fold(0_u64, u64::saturating_add)
    21	                    .saturating_mul(8),
    22	            )
    23	            .saturating_add(if source.is_expiring() || (self.device && maintain.parent_key.is_some()) {
    24	                row_copy_ceiling(source).saturating_mul(32)
    25	            } else {
    26	                0
    27	            })
    28	    }

    30	    /// A maintain over expiring source rows is a live fact before the
    31	    /// physical sweep catches up. Recompute only that fact's group, with
    32	    /// the usual runtime meter and device coverage rules.
    33	    pub(crate) fn live_aggregate(
    34	        &mut self,
    35	        table_name: &str,
    36	        row: Value,
    37	    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
    38	        self.aggregate_source_dependency(table_name);
    39	        let Some(maintain) = self.schema.maintain_for(table_name) else {
    40	            return Ok(Some(row));
    41	        };
    42	        // @ref LLP 3000.015#3 — a row-keyed count certifies its live basis on the internal ledger.
    43	        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.live_row_view(maintain, row); }
    44	        if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) && self.receipt_maintain_pending(maintain, Some(&crate::schema::maintained_key(&row, &maintain.by)))? { return Ok(Some(row)); }
    45	        let source = self
    46	            .schema
    47	            .table(&maintain.source)
    48	            .ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema("missing maintain source".into()))?;
    49	        if !source.is_expiring() {
    50	            return Ok(Some(row));
    51	        }
    52	        let bytes = super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(source)
    53	            .saturating_mul(32)
    54	            .saturating_add(
    55	                super::write_target::row_copy_ceiling(&self.schema.tables[table_name])
    56	                    .saturating_mul(16),
    57	            );
    58	        self.maintain_scratch(bytes, |runner| runner.live_aggregate_inner(maintain, row))
    59	    }

    61	    /// A maintained point read reserved its recount scratch up front
    62	    /// (`aggregate_point_scratch`); recompute without a second reservation.
    63	    pub(super) fn live_aggregate_prepaid(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Value) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
    64	        self.aggregate_source_dependency(table_name);
    65	        let Some(maintain) = self.schema.maintain_for(table_name) else { return Ok(Some(row)); };
    66	        if maintain.row_key.is_some() { return self.live_row_view(maintain, row); }
    67	        if self.defer_receipt_maintain(maintain) && self.receipt_maintain_pending(maintain, Some(&crate::schema::maintained_key(&row, &maintain.by)))? { return Ok(Some(row)); }
    68	        if !self.schema.tables[&maintain.source].is_expiring() { return Ok(Some(row)); }
    69	        self.live_aggregate_inner(maintain, row)
    70	    }

    80	    pub(super) fn live_aggregate_inner(
    81	        &mut self,
    82	        maintain: &crate::schema::Maintain,
    83	        row: Value,
    84	    ) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {

    97	        let (index, prefix) = maintain.source_scan(source, &group);
    98	        if self.device
    99	            && source

/-- Truncating quotient/remainder followed by one exact rounding step. The
model deliberately derives truncation from the existing Euclidean primitive,
so its oracle is independent of the Rust implementation. -/
def roundedDiv (rounding : Rounding) (scale : Option Nat) (x y : Int) : EM Value := do
  if y = 0 then refuse "E_DIV_ZERO"
  let x := x * (10 : Int) ^ scale.getD 0
  let qe := Int.ediv x y
  let re := Int.emod x y
  let q := if x < 0 ∧ re ≠ 0 then qe + (if y < 0 then -1 else 1) else qe
  let r := x - q * y
  if r = 0 then checkI53 q else
    let direction : Int := if (x < 0) = (y < 0) then 1 else -1
    let away := q + direction
    let result := match rounding with
      | .towardZero => q
      | .awayFromZero => away
      | .floor => if direction < 0 then away else q
      | .ceiling => if 0 < direction then away else q
      | .halfAwayFromZero => if Int.natAbs r * 2 ≥ Int.natAbs y then away else q
      | .halfEven =>
          if Int.natAbs r * 2 > Int.natAbs y ∨
              (Int.natAbs r * 2 = Int.natAbs y ∧ Int.emod q 2 ≠ 0)
          then away else q
    checkI53 result

/-- A calendar builtin over unbounded integers; the caller checks i53. A
non-positive period or an offset outside `[0, period)` is unreachable from a
checked program. -/
def calApply : CalFn → Int → Option Int
  t[..]` (a row that must exist by the end of the mutation that inserted
  this one).

- **Sync** (`guide sync`) and **retain**: `retain until-revoked` (the default: a
  device drops a group's rows when it leaves the group) or
  `retain delivered-history` (it keeps what it was given).
- **Expire:** `expire at .expiresAt` makes a row absent at its deadline.
  `guide expire` covers physical cleanup and caps.
  Held device observations republish at the deadline, including offline.
  Server-answered reads use `client.now()` and `useNow(deadline)` to hide rows
  while their next answer is pending (`guide reads`).
  This is an application table, separate from the server's `connected[p]`.
  That server-decided connection signal has no `expiresAt`.
  The server will not return it again after expiry, but does not push a
  removal at that instant.
  A null time never expires. Disappearing messages
  are one field on insert, `expiresAt: now + ttl if ttl != null else
  null` with `ttl: int ?`; nothing else to write.

fn compile(tail: &str) -> snapback4_lang::Bound {
    snapback4_lang::compile(&[("maintains.q".into(), format!("{SOURCE}\n{tail}"))])
}

#[test]
fn length_alias_keeps_calendar_duration_units() {
    let b = compile("query guessed():\n  return len([day(now, 8h), bucket(now, 1d, 8h)])\n");
    assert!(b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
    let fixed = compile("query guessed():\n  return count([day(now, 8h), bucket(now, 1d, 8h)])\n");
    assert_eq!(b.programs[0].program, fixed.programs[0].program);
}

#[test]
fn calendar_offsets_preserve_zero_forms_and_refuse_outside_the_period() {
    for (plain, zero) in [("day(.at)", "day(.at, 0ms)"), ("hour(.at)", "hour(.at, 0s)"), ("bucket(.at, 2m)", "bucket(.at, 2m, 0m)")] {
        let program = |form: &str| format!("maintain totals: count posts by author, {form}\n  read <- allow\n  online only\nquery key():\n  return {}\n", form.replace(".at", "now"));
        let a = compile(&program(plain)); let b = compile(&program(zero));
        assert!(a.diagnostics.is_empty() && b.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", b.diagnostics);
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&a.schema).unwrap(), serde_json::to_value(&b.schema).unwrap());
        assert_eq!(serde_json::to_value(&a.programs[0].program).unwrap(), serde_json::to_value(&b.programs[0].program).unwrap());
        let key = &a.schema.maintains[0].computed.values().next().unwrap();
        let encoded = serde_json::to_value(key).unwrap();
